items.title: A24's Elizabeth Holmes 'You Can See Everything' Documentary Crosses the $100 Million USD Mark
items.summary:
Summary 

A24's hit documentary 'You Can See Everything' has officially surpassed the $100 million USD mark at the global box officeThe secretly produced Elizabeth Holmes film has generated $93.4 million USD domestically alongside a growing international rolloutThe massive financial milestone cements the nearly three-hour project as one of the highest-grossing theatrical documentaries in history

A24 and its hit documentary You Can See Everything have officially crossed a massive theatrical milestone. Surpassing $100 million USD at the global box office, the zeitgeist-capturing look at Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes has generated a staggering $93.4 million USD domestically and $9 million USD overseas for a worldwide tally of $102.4 million USD.

Produced in secret for roughly $7 million USD, the nearly three-hour-long film directed by comedian Nathan Fielder and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim takes place over three years. The narrative begins as Holmes prepares for her 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors, transforming into a word-of-mouth smash following a surprise premiere at the Telluride Film Festival. The documentary initially opened to $15 million USD domestically in mid-October and has remained a dominant big-screen draw driven by strong reviews and a demographic that is overwhelmingly under 35 years old.

Currently rolling out internationally, the film just marked A24's second-largest debut in the United Kingdom with $3.2 million USD. Australia and New Zealand currently stand as the top-grossing overseas markets with $3.8 million USD, while a handful of…
items.t: A24's Elizabeth Holmes 'You Can See Everything' Documentary Crosses the $100 Million USD Mark

items.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
items.summary:
Summary 

Jensen Huang has been officially reinstated as the CEO of Nvidia following unanimous board approvalThe abrupt reversal comes after prominent tech figures and government officials lobbied for his returnShares of the massive chipmaker skyrocketed 35% immediately following the reinstatement announcement

Nvidia has officially reinstated Jensen Huang as its Chief Executive Officer, ending a highly turbulent period for the artificial intelligence giant. Effective immediately, the dramatic leadership reversal arrives less than two weeks after the visionary co-founder stepped down amidst an extramarital scandal, sending shockwaves through the global tech sector and severely hammering the company's market valuation.

The board of directors unanimously voted to bring Huang back to the helm after a series of intense weekend meetings. Following his initial resignation on November 13, which stemmed from reports of an affair involving an alleged Chinese spy, Nvidia's stock plummeted nearly 33%. However, the landscape shifted rapidly when senior United States government officials briefed the board, explicitly confirming that Huang's return posed no national security risk and that no laws were violated. Consequently, shares of the chipmaker surged an astonishing 35% following the Monday announcement.

The reinstatement was heavily championed by massive industry players and political figures alike. Tech leaders including SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner, and Atreides Management CIO Gavin Baker actively lobbied for Huang's return. President Donald Trump…
items.t: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

items.title: What Went Down at CYBEX’s Platinum S-Line Launch With Nico Rosberg
items.summary:
On October 13, CYBEX opened the doors of its headquarters in Bayreuth, Germany, to officially welcome Nico Rosberg as its new Child Safety Ambassador. The Formula 1 World Champion and venture capital entrepreneur used the occasion to help unveil the brand’s latest launch, the Platinum S-Line of car seats.

International media, content creators and associations filled the space, alongside guests from the worlds of automotive, technology and innovation. The centerpiece was a panel talk in which Rosberg sat down with CYBEX founder Martin Pos and motorsport presenter and TV host Nicki Shields. They discussed pushing boundaries in safety, the role of intelligent technology in everyday family life, and how innovation can put advanced safety within easier reach for parents.

For Rosberg, the connection is personal. “In Formula 1, you learn that the safety work nobody sees is often the work that matters most. Becoming a father gave that mindset a whole new meaning for me,” he said. “What excites me about CYBEX is its relentless drive to challenge what is possible through technology, innovation and design. We share the belief that safety should never stand still, and I am proud to join CYBEX in bringing this conversation to a wider audience.”

Pos returned the sentiment. “Nico is a natural fit for CYBEX,” he said. “His career has been defined by a constant pursuit of innovation and performance. Together, we want to explore how technology can make a meaningful difference to the safety of children and families, and inspire people to think differently about what the future of child…

items.title: TOMORROW X TOGETHER Find Upheaval Worth Running Toward on 'PERFECT STORM'
items.summary:
A line in "Angel Bite" is "Even love costs money," and it's about as blunt as TOMORROW X TOGETHER have ever been. Taehyun says that's on purpose. Over the years, the group has written different versions of this song, penning metaphors to express what it's like to hold on to someone you have nothing to give. This time around, he says they wanted to "strip down all the romanticized notions of youth and actually confront the anxiety, pain, and sense of deprivation underneath it." Another line on the song pushes it further: "Ain't got nothing, so how am I supposed to afford a future?"

The intentionality runs across the entirety of PERFECT STORM . Their latest project arrives only only seven months after 7TH YEAR: A Moment of Stillness in the Thorns , and shifts the focus from 7TH YEAR's anxieties to what they did next. "For us, a storm isn't an obstacle to fight against, but a catalyst for change that sweeps away the stagnant air and opens doors to new possibilities," Taehyun explains. "We definitely felt the need for change, and this album is our way of diving headfirst into that whirlwind of transformation."

Soobin reveals the storm wasn't the plan from the start. When they first sat down, the only thing everyone agreed on was that they needed to do "something completely different" from what they've done before. The storm idea came later, as they worked it through with their team. What he talks about more is what happened once they started writing. "In the beginning, all the anxieties we had felt massive and uncontrollable, almost like we were bracing ourselves for an…
items.t: TOMORROW X TOGETHER Find Upheaval Worth Running Toward on 'PERFECT STORM'

items.title: American Airlines and Alpha Industries Reimagine the MA-1 Flight Jacket for Airline’s 100th Anniversary
items.summary:
American Airlines has teamed up with Alpha Industries to celebrate its 100th anniversary with a limited-edition MA-1 Flight Jacket, transforming leather reclaimed from retired aircraft seats into a wearable piece of aviation history.

Spearheaded by creative agency Ceeze, the collaboration brings together American Airlines’ archival heritage and Alpha Industries’ iconic MA-1 silhouette. Rather than relying on conventional fabrics, the project repurposes authentic upholstery from American Airlines’ retired fleet. Each jacket is handcrafted in New York City, with the reclaimed leather carefully cut, rearranged and reconstructed into a distinctive patchwork design. Only 100 pieces will be produced worldwide.

Design-wise, the jacket features a dark blue leather exterior complemented by a red satin lining, silver zipper and graphite-colored ribbed cuffs. An American Airlines logo patch dating back to the 1930s completes the design, paying homage to the airline’s century-long history.

Originally developed as functional military outerwear, the MA-1 Flight Jacket has since transcended its utilitarian origins, becoming a staple across youth subcultures, streetwear and high fashion. This latest collaboration reconnects the silhouette with its aviation roots, giving authentic aircraft materials a second life while offering a fresh interpretation of an enduring wardrobe icon.

The American Airlines x Alpha Industries 100th Anniversary MA-1 Flight Jacket has officially been unveiled, with further release details yet to be announced.

Of the 100 jackets made, American Airlines plans…
items.t: American Airlines and Alpha Industries Reimagine the MA-1 Flight Jacket for Airline’s 100th Anniversary

items.title: Brioche armchairs, butter sculptures and edible chandeliers: meet the new food artists
items.summary:
Culinary artists are turning fashion shows and design fairs into a feast for the eyes

A pretty Venetian chandelier featuring delicate pink flowers and cascading blue leaves hangs from a ceiling. A hazy, warm light radiates from its tulip bulbs. Suddenly, a woman reaches up and snaps off one of the flower stems, giggling as she begins to nibble it. Welcome to the weird and wonderful world of Laila Gohar. The Egyptian-born, New York-based artist is part of a new wave of culinary artists blurring the lines between sustenance and spectacle, and this troupe have quickly become a firm fixture at fashion parties and design fairs, turning dining into a phenomenon and delight.

Gohar describes the chandelier, made entirely from hand-spun sugar (including the silver chain that suspended it) as her “favourite thing she has done in recent history”. It joins a long list of extravagant yet still edible installations she has created, including lifesize armchairs made of brioche, an entire room constructed with Belgian chocolate and a four-metre-long mortadella that had to be lifted into the party’s venue using a crane.

Jeff Staple has officially announced the closure of his Staple 21 Mercer retail store in New York City . Taking over the former NikeLab space in SoHo, the destination operated as a vibrant retail and cultural hub for 20 months, with its final day of operation officially set for Friday, November 27.

Reflecting on the space's tenure, the brand emphasized that the location was always intended to be more than just a traditional retail storefront. Built as a cultural gathering place where community came before commerce, Staple 21 Mercer frequently welcomed creatives and innovators across the spheres of music, art, sports, and gaming. The brand's founder noted that the most memorable moments of the store's run were entirely unplanned, capturing the serendipitous spirit of New York City. Employees similarly echoed the sentiment, expressing gratitude for the connections built and legends met during the store's operations.

While the physical address is shutting its doors, the Staple brand and its iconic Pigeon logo are shifting strategies rather than slowing down. items.title: Ferrari Sheds Hybrid Tech to Create the Ultimate V6 Track Monster
items.summary:
Summary 

The new Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale drops its hybrid system.Shedding 310 pounds, the 670-horsepower V6 delivers pure analog speed.Massive aero and a stripped carbon-fiber cabin maximize track performance.

Ferrari has officially unveiled its latest track-focused weapon, the Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale. Arriving 23 years after the original 360 Challenge Stradale, this new iteration strips away the hybrid system to reduce weight and deliver an analog experience. 

At the heart of the 296 Challenge Stradale sits a tuned 3.0-liter, 120-degree twin-turbo V6 engine. Without the electric motor, the engine produces 670 horsepower at 8,000 rpm and 546 lb-ft of torque, sending power exclusively to the rear wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission. Dropping the hybrid hardware sheds significant bulk, resulting in a dry weight of just 2,932 pounds, nearly 310 pounds lighter than the GTB. This diet allows the car to launch from zero to 62 mph in just 2.8 seconds and reach a top speed in excess of 186 mph. Around Ferrari’s famed Fiorano test track, it clocks a blistering lap time of 1:18.5, beating the likes of the LaFerrari and SF90 .

Visually, the car leans heavily into its motorsport roots. The GTB ’s active spoiler has been replaced with a massive fixed rear wing, which helps generate over 1,360 pounds of downforce at 155 mph. A newly designed twin-exit exhaust system minimizes back pressure while amplifying the V6’s high-pitched wail. To harness the immense grip, Ferrari has equipped the car with recalibrated semi-active suspension, carbon-ceramic brakes,…

Unveiled in Lake Como, the collection serves as a statement of identity and sophistication, marrying Brioni’s Made-in-Italy sartorial savoir-faire with Como 1907’s contemporary football aesthetic.

items.title: In a flap: how the butterfly became a symbol of gen Z resilience – and anxiety
items.summary:
The delicate insect has become fashion’s favourite motif again – but having represented sexuality in the 90s and the soul in Greco-Roman times, what does it say about youth culture today?

• Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

In the new Gucci campaign, Mariah Carey blows a goodbye kiss to 2026 in the most Mariahhhh way possible. Dressed in a fake fur coat and an azure dress, she enters a Christmas party to the twinkly sounds of All I Want For Christmas Is You. There are beautiful people, presents wrapped with Gucci string and butterflies, which have been associated with the popstar since her 1997 album, Butterfly, but have recently fluttered back to become a symbol of gen Z defiance and girlhood.

Carey serves as fairy godmother to the other “pop girlies” who have embraced the emblem, from PinkPantheress to Dua Lipa; Rachel Chinouriri to Marina and the Diamonds. At the Academy Museum gala in October, the singer Janelle Monáe looked as if she might take flight in a Robert Wun couture gown, with wide, yonic wings. Elsewhere, Tate McRae recently wore a black sequined butterfly bra and matching butterfly wing belt from lingerie wunderkind Ludovic de Saint Sernin. Both Swedish popstar Zara Larsson and her fans are championing glittery butterfly makeup motifs.
items.t: In a flap: how the butterfly became a symbol of gen Z resilience – and anxiety
